records.title: California's Fish and Game Commission to vote on 15 marine protected area petitions as two state agencies disagree
records.description: California's network of 124 marine protected areas covers about 16% of state waters. The Fish and Game Commission received 20 petitions in December 2023 proposing more than 80 changes, approved five in 2025 and is set to hear the remaining 15 on 15 and 16 October. The Department of Fish and Wildlife recommended denial, while the Ocean Protection Council recommended approving proposals that strengthen the network, including a tribally co-led nine-acre Mishopshno MPA at Carpinteria that local fishers oppose.

records.title: More than 1,000 dead olive ridley turtles wash ashore on Chennai's beaches in January 2025
records.description: Over 1,000 dead olive ridley turtles washed up along Chennai's coast over several weeks of January 2025, including 346 recorded by volunteers on the 13 km between Neelankarai and Marina Beach, the highest monthly toll for the city. Conservationists pointed to drowning in trawler nets and trawlers working inside the five nautical mile limit; the official post-mortem had not been released at the time of reporting. The National Green Tribunal's southern bench warned of a complete trawling ban in the nesting season and the Fisheries Department mandated turtle excluder devices.

notes.livelihoods: The Fisheries Department mandated turtle excluder devices for trawlers and began patrols inside five nautical miles, and fishers said enforcement and subsidy withdrawal hit them (refs 1, 2).
notes.scale: The deaths were counted along the Chennai coastline, with the volunteer count covering a 13 km stretch (ref 1).
notes.duration: The die-off was concentrated in a few weeks of January 2025, though experts note olive ridleys die every year and only about 20 percent of dead turtles wash ashore (ref 1).

records.title: Record olive ridley arribada of about 700,000 turtles at Rushikulya in February 2025
records.description: Odisha forest officials counted 698,718 olive ridley turtles nesting at Rushikulya between 16 and 23 February 2025, surpassing the 637,000 recorded in 2023, and scientists who have monitored the site for 20 years called it the biggest arribada they have documented. The beach is not a protected area and was guarded by forest staff and villagers, and scientists said the population appears healthy, while noting coastal erosion and development as continuing concerns. The site had no arribada in 2024.

records.title: Gahirmatha mass nesting fails in 2026 as erosion pushes the olive ridley rookery 14 km north
records.description: Gahirmatha beach in Odisha, described as the world's largest olive ridley rookery, saw no synchronised mass nesting in the 2026 season, with only sporadic nesting reported between the Devi and Dhamra river mouths. A satellite study of 1990 to 2022 found the nesting ground has shifted about 14 km northwards because of coastal erosion, with the highest erosion in 2020-21 coinciding with a roughly 50 percent fall in mass nesting. Experts quoted attribute the 2026 absence to changing ecological conditions and climate change, and the cause has not been established.

notes.duration: The erosion study spans 1990 to 2022 and mass nesting was low in 2023 and 2024 as well, at 31,115 and 66,933 turtles per the Forest Department figures cited (refs 1, 2).
notes.significance: Gahirmatha was declared a marine sanctuary in 1997 and carries the annual fishing restriction, a formal protected-area regime in place (ref 1).

records.title: Coral bleaching across Thailand's Andaman marine parks closes Phi Phi dive and snorkel sites for almost a year
records.description: Thailand's Department of National Parks reported coral bleaching in 19 marine park areas between 2 April and 8 May 2024, 11 of them on the Andaman Sea coast including Similan, Surin, Phi Phi, Lanta and Phetra, with more than 80 percent bleaching at Pling Island in Sirinat National Park. The Hat Noppharat Thara-Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park closed several dive and snorkel sites on 13 May 2024 and reopened ten sites in April 2025 after assessments showed strong recovery, while the west side of Koh Gai stayed closed.

records.title: Bangladesh limits visitors to Saint Martin's Island, then bars tourist vessels for nine months in 2026 to protect its coral
records.description: Bangladesh's government announced in October 2024 that tourism to Saint Martin's Island, the country's only coral island, would be limited because visitor pressure was polluting the island and stressing its coral, citing that only 41 percent of coral remains. On 1 February 2026 tourist vessels were barred for nine months after a shortened 2025-26 season. The Department of Environment reported healthier reefs, returning sea turtles and more sea snails in 2025, while tour operators and residents warned of lost income.

records.title: Chilika's Irrawaddy dolphin count stays flat at 159 in the January 2026 census
records.description: The Odisha Forest Department's 20 January 2026 census counted 765 dolphins of six species along the state's coast, but only 159 Irrawaddy dolphins in Chilika Lake, a number reporters describe as flat for two years. Experts attribute the stagnation to slow breeding and habitat stress from large prawn gheries and nylon fishing nets. Chilika hosts the largest known single-habitat Irrawaddy dolphin population in the world.

notes.livelihoods: No fishery restriction is described in the cited census reports (refs 1, 2).
notes.scale: The population sits in one lagoon, Chilika Lake (ref 2).
notes.duration: The count was 154 Irrawaddy dolphins in the January 2023 survey and 159 in 2026, so the population has been stagnant over several years (refs 2, 3).
notes.significance: The Irrawaddy dolphin is listed Endangered by the IUCN according to the lake's reference entry, and the Forest Department runs an annual formal census (refs 1, 4).

records.title: Dar es Salaam beaches and rivers carry marine litter, higher in the wet season, with 70% of it made locally
records.description: A peer-reviewed study of litter sampled in 2019-2021 counted 127,658 items weighing 470 kg on Dar es Salaam beaches and 1,365 items in two rivers. Litter densities were significantly higher in the wet season, which the authors attribute to river transport of plastics, and 70% of the litter was produced locally. Marine litter density fell by 61% over the three years of the study, but the authors call for a policy to cut marine litter.

records.title: Metal bioaccumulation found in Dar es Salaam mangroves nearest the city centre
records.description: A TAFIRI study of sediments, water, invertebrates and mangrove leaves along the Dar es Salaam coast and at Mbegani found metal bioaccumulation, mostly at sites close to the city centre, decreasing with distance. The non-essential metals named include aluminium, copper, iron, manganese and zinc. The authors identify Avicennia marina leaves and two invertebrates as suitable local biomonitors.

records.title: Grounded vessels off Nyali and Kikambala prompt oil and chemical pollution fears on Kenya's north coast
records.description: MV Adan ran aground on a coral reef off Nyali beach, Mombasa, on 18 May 2026, and the Kenya Maritime Authority said refloating would begin in mid-August 2026 while maritime sources warned of possible fuel discharge. Separately, Kikambala residents in Kilifi County alleged oil and chemical spills from salvage of the wrecked cement carrier MV Jozani II, with dead marine animals and halted fishing; no official response was quoted. Both items come from newspaper reports of July 2026.

notes.significance: The KMA statement is oversight of a salvage plan, not a pollution order, and no regulator confirmation of leaks was quoted (ref 2).

records.title: Kenya-Tanzania border flagged as an oil pollution hotspot as the Western Indian Ocean finalises a regional spill plan
records.description: A study by the Indian Ocean Commission, reported in July 2025, named the Kenya-Tanzania border near Mombasa and Dar es Salaam as one of seven hotspots for oil pollution from ships. Kenya ran a five-day response exercise in Mombasa on 7-11 July 2025, and in January 2026 experts from ten countries met in Zanzibar under the Nairobi Convention to finalise a Regional Contingency Plan.
